source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus publishes 114 megawatts of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in Illinois and 48 percent of the state's published total.

The pattern is that power disclosure is rare and highly concentrated. Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and only six with published power figures, so one three-building campus accounts for nearly half of what is publicly known about the state's capacity. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 114 megawatts translates to roughly 2,850 racks. Spread across 450,000 square feet, that is about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet, which is ordinary for hyperscale colocation built in the last decade rather than a design aimed at accelerator clusters.

For AI, the number that matters is not the campus total but how much of it can reach dense racks and stay there. The published specifications include nothing on power delivery tier, redundancy topology, cooling technology, or cooling source. Green Globes certification speaks to environmental accounting, not to whether the site can hold a training workload.

What is missing is the binding constraint. There are no figures for total campus draw, PUE, renewable sourcing, grid connection characteristics, or uplinks to cloud regions. Whether Aurora's 114 megawatts limits AI scaling in Illinois or is simply a large colocation footprint depends on facts the operator has not disclosed.
